item.title: [British Journal of Anaesthesia] Postoperative changes in cardiovascular metrics and adverse clinical outcomes after major noncardiac surgery: a scoping review
item.description: Cardiovascular metrics such as HR and BP reflect autonomic and haemodynamic regulation and are associated with perioperative risk. In noncardiac surgery, most work focuses on the intraoperative period or broad perioperative BP management, rather than the immediate postoperative period as a distinct window of vulnerability. The early postoperative period is characterised by residual anaesthetic effects, pain, fluid shifts, bleeding risk, inflammatory stress, mobilisation, and changing monitoring intensity.

item.title: [British Journal of Anaesthesia] Bleeding management in cardiac surgery: a simplified, goal-directed algorithm using conventional coagulation assays
item.description: Excessive bleeding remains a major challenge in cardiac surgery despite advances in perioperative bleeding management, including the adoption of viscoelastic haemostatic assay (VHA)-guided algorithms. We propose an alternative, streamlined approach that primarily uses familiar, low-cost coagulation assays to rapidly identify and treat the principal post-cardiopulmonary bypass coagulation defects, reserving VHA for refractory bleeding, and prioritises factor concentrates as first-line therapy instead of allogeneic blood products.
